The machine has separate private 32-bit and 64-bit register banks.
`mul.wide.u32` reads two unsigned 32-bit operands and writes their full 64-bit
product. `add.u64` adds two 64-bit operands modulo `2^64`. Operands are read
from the incoming state before the destination is written. Each instruction
advances the program counter and preserves the other registers. These rules
follow NVIDIA's [integer multiplication](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.0.1/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#integer-arithmetic-instructions-mul)
and [integer addition](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.0.1/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#integer-arithmetic-instructions-add)
descriptions.

passage.quote:
/-- The full unsigned product of two 32-bit words fits in 64 bits. -/
def wideProduct (a b : Word32) : Word64 :=
  BitVec.ofNat 64 (a.toNat * b.toNat)

@[simp] theorem wideProduct_toNat (a b : Word32) :
    (wideProduct a b).toNat = a.toNat * b.toNat := by
  exact Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (BitVec.toNat_mul_toNat_lt (x := a) (y := b))

/-- Immutable special-register values supplied to one thread. -/
structure Identity where
  tidX : Word32
  ctaidX : Word32

/-- One thread's private registers/PC, together with the shared global-memory snapshot. -/
structure State (Reg : Type) where
  regs : Reg → Word32
  pc : Nat
  regs64 : Reg → Word64
  globalMemory : GlobalMemory
  predicates : Reg → Bool := fun _ => false
  returned : Bool := false

inductive Operand (Reg : Type) where
  | reg (name : Reg)
  | imm (value : Word32)
  | tidX
  | ctaidX

def Operand.read (id : Identity) (s : State Reg) : Operand Reg → Word32
  | .reg r => s.regs r
  | .imm v => v
  | .tidX => id.tidX
  | .ctaidX => id.ctaidX

inductive Operand64 (Reg : Type) where
  | reg (name : Reg)
  | imm (value : Word64)

def Operand64.read (s : State Reg) : Operand64 Reg → Word64
  | .reg r => s.regs64 r
  | .imm v => v

/-- Selected instruction forms needed by the scalar dense-ReLU kernel. -/
inductive Instruction (Reg : Type) where
  | mov (dst : Reg) (src : Operand Reg)
  | madLo (dst : Reg) (a b c : Operand Reg)
  | mulWide (dst : Reg) (a b : Operand Reg)
  | add64 (dst : Reg) (a b : Operand64 Reg)
  | ldParam64 (dst : Reg) (symbol : String)
  | cvtaGlobal64 (dst : Reg) (src : Operand64 Reg)
  | movF32 (dst : Reg) (value : Word32)
  | loadF32 (dst : Reg) (address : Operand64 Reg)
  | fmaRN (dst : Reg) (a b c : Operand Reg)
  | add32 (dst : Reg) (a b : Operand Reg)
  | setpLt (dst : Reg) (a b : Operand Reg)
  | branchIf (predicate : Reg) (target : Nat)
  | addF32RN (dst : Reg) (a b : Operand Reg)
  | maxPositiveZero (dst : Reg) (src : Operand Reg)
  | storeF32 (address : Operand64 Reg) (src : Operand Reg)
  | ret

def State.write [DecidableEq Reg] (s : State Reg) (dst : Reg) (v : Word32) : State Reg :=
  { s with regs := fun r => if r = dst then v else s.regs r, pc := s.pc + 1 }

def State.write64 [DecidableEq Reg] (s : State Reg) (dst : Reg) (v : Word64) : State Reg :=
  { s with regs64 := fun r => if r = dst then v else s.regs64 r, pc := s.pc + 1 }

/-- All operands are read before the destination is updated. BitVec arithmetic wraps. -/
def Instruction.execute [DecidableEq Reg] (id : Identity) (s : State Reg)
    (inst : Instruction Reg) (env : Environment := Environment.empty)
    (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic := none) : Option (State Reg) :=
  match inst with
  | .mov dst src => some (s.write dst (src.read id s))
  | .madLo dst a b c => some (s.write dst (a.read id s * b.read id s + c.read id s))
  | .mulWide dst a b => some (s.write64 dst (wideProduct (a.read id s) (b.read id s)))
  | .add64 dst a b => some (s.write64 dst (a.read s + b.read s))
  | .ldParam64 dst symbol => (env.params symbol).map (s.write64 dst)
  | .cvtaGlobal64 dst src => (env.space.toGlobal (src.read s)).map (s.write64 dst)
  | .movF32 dst value => some (s.write dst value)
  | .loadF32 dst address => (s.globalMemory (address.read s)).map (s.write dst)
  | .fmaRN dst a b c => ops.map (fun op =>
      s.write dst (op.fmaRN (a.read id s) (b.read id s) (c.read id s)))
  | .add32 dst a b => some (s.write dst (a.read id s + b.read id s))
  | .setpLt dst a b => some { s with
      predicates := fun r => if r = dst then decide ((a.read id s).toNat < (b.read id s).toNat)
        else s.predicates r
      pc := s.pc + 1 }
  | .branchIf predicate target => some { s with
      pc := if s.predicates predicate then target else s.pc + 1 }
  | .addF32RN dst a b => ops.map (fun op =>
      s.write dst (op.addRN (a.read id s) (b.read id s)))
  | .maxPositiveZero dst src => some (s.write dst (FP32.maxPositiveZero (src.read id s)))
  | .storeF32 address src => some { s with
      globalMemory := fun a => if a = address.read s then some (src.read id s) else s.globalMemory a
      pc := s.pc + 1 }
  | .ret => some { s with returned := true, pc := s.pc + 1 }

/-- Active threads fetch at the current PC; returned threads have no next step. -/
def step [DecidableEq Reg] (program : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity)
    (s : State Reg) (env : Environment := Environment.empty)
    (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic := none) : Option (State Reg) :=
  if s.returned then none else
    (program[s.pc]?).bind (fun inst => inst.execute id s env ops)

/-- Execute exactly `fuel` instructions; failed fetches and excluded instruction uses yield `none`. -/
def run [DecidableEq Reg] (program : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity)
    (fuel : Nat) (s : State Reg) (env : Environment := Environment.empty)
    (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic := none) : Option (State Reg) :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => some s
  | fuel + 1 => (step program id s env ops).bind (fun next => run program id fuel next env ops)

theorem run_add [DecidableEq Reg] (program : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity)
    (a b : Nat) (s : State Reg) (env : Environment) (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic) :
    run program id (a + b) s env ops =
      (run program id a s env ops).bind (fun next => run program id b next env ops) := by
  induction a generalizing s with
  | zero => simp [run]
  | succ a ih => simp [Nat.succ_add, run, ih, Option.bind_assoc]

private theorem step_append_of_step [DecidableEq Reg]
    (program suffix : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity) (s next : State Reg)
    (env : Environment) (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic)
    (h : step program id s env ops = some next) :
    step (program ++ suffix) id s env ops = some next := by
  have hpc : s.pc < program.length := by
    by_contra hn
    have hf := List.getElem?_eq_none (l := program) (by omega : program.length ≤ s.pc)
    simp [step, hf] at h
  simpa only [step, List.getElem?_append_left hpc] using h

/-- Appending instructions cannot change an already successful prefix execution. -/
theorem run_append_of_run [DecidableEq Reg]
    (program suffix : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity) (fuel : Nat)
    (s final : State Reg) (env : Environment) (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic)
    (h : run program id fuel s env ops = some final) :
    run (program ++ suffix) id fuel s env ops = some final := by
  induction fuel generalizing s with
  | zero => simpa [run] using h
  | succ fuel ih =>
    obtain ⟨next, hs, ht⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp h
    have he := step_append_of_step program suffix id s next env ops hs
    simpa only [run, he, Option.bind_some] using ih next ht

The layer specializes the width to 1024 and the row count to the configured
launch's 3072 rows. The five formal instructions are compared with the exact
PTX source fragment by an executable source check. The correspondence checker
is not a proved parser. Base-address initialization and conversion, actual

private def instructionText : Instruction Register → String := Instruction.ptxText

def main (args : List String) : IO Unit := do
  let source ← IO.FS.readFile (args.headD "kernels/relu_layer.ptx")
  let normalized := "\n" ++ String.intercalate "\n"
    ((source.splitOn "\n").map (fun line => line.trimAscii.toString))
  let expected := "\n" ++ String.intercalate "\n"
    ((addressCalculation layerLayout.inputWidth).map instructionText) ++ "\n"
  unless (normalized.splitOn expected).length == 2 do
    throw (IO.userError s!"Expected exactly one address fragment:\n{expected}")
  IO.println "Five address instructions match the formal layout and register operands."

base-address registers for weights, bias, and output. It executes two wide
multiplies and three additions through instruction fetches and register
updates. For arbitrary initial scratch registers, its final program counter
is five, the row, base registers, input pointer, and global-memory snapshot are

W_{\mathrm{read}}=W_{\mathrm{base}}+i\,(\mathrm{inputWidth}\cdot4),

/-- FP32 storage size in bytes. -/
def fp32Bytes : Nat := 4

/-- The layout supplies the input width; the row stride is derived from it. -/
structure Layout where
  inputWidth : Nat
  inputWidth_pos : 0 < inputWidth
  stride_fits : inputWidth * fp32Bytes < 2 ^ 32

def Layout.rowStride (layout : Layout) : Nat := layout.inputWidth * fp32Bytes

/-- Exactly the two offset multiplies and three pointer additions in the kernel. -/
def addressCalculation (inputWidth : Nat) : List (Instruction Register) :=
  [ .mulWide .rowOffset (.reg .row) (.imm (BitVec.ofNat 32 (inputWidth * fp32Bytes))),
    .mulWide .elementOffset (.reg .row) (.imm (BitVec.ofNat 32 fp32Bytes)),
    .add64 .weightRead (.reg .weightBase) (.reg .rowOffset),
    .add64 .biasRead (.reg .biasBase) (.reg .elementOffset),
    .add64 .outputWrite (.reg .outputBase) (.reg .elementOffset) ]

private def finalState (width : Nat) (initial : State Register) : State Register :=
  let s := initial.write64 .rowOffset
    (wideProduct (initial.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 (width * fp32Bytes)))
  let s := s.write64 .elementOffset
    (wideProduct (s.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 fp32Bytes))
  let s := s.write64 .weightRead (s.regs64 .weightBase + s.regs64 .rowOffset)
  let s := s.write64 .biasRead (s.regs64 .biasBase + s.regs64 .elementOffset)
  s.write64 .outputWrite (s.regs64 .outputBase + s.regs64 .elementOffset)

/-- Word-level execution facts hold even when pointer addition wraps. -/
structure AddressWords (width : Nat) (initial final : State Register) : Prop where
  pc : final.pc = 5
  regs32 : final.regs = initial.regs
  memory : final.globalMemory = initial.globalMemory
  predicates : final.predicates = initial.predicates
  active : final.returned = initial.returned
  inputRead : final.regs64 .inputRead = initial.regs64 .inputRead
  weightBase : final.regs64 .weightBase = initial.regs64 .weightBase
  biasBase : final.regs64 .biasBase = initial.regs64 .biasBase
  outputBase : final.regs64 .outputBase = initial.regs64 .outputBase
  rowOffset : final.regs64 .rowOffset =
    wideProduct (initial.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 (width * fp32Bytes))
  elementOffset : final.regs64 .elementOffset =
    wideProduct (initial.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 fp32Bytes)
  weights : final.regs64 .weightRead = initial.regs64 .weightBase +
    wideProduct (initial.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 (width * fp32Bytes))
  bias : final.regs64 .biasRead = initial.regs64 .biasBase +
    wideProduct (initial.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 fp32Bytes)
  output : final.regs64 .outputWrite = initial.regs64 .outputBase +
    wideProduct (initial.regs .row) (BitVec.ofNat 32 fp32Bytes)

theorem addressCalculation_exec (width : Nat) (id : Identity)
    (initial : State Register) (hpc : initial.pc = 0) (env : Environment) (hactive : initial.returned = false)
    (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic := none) :
    ∃ final, run (addressCalculation width) id 5 initial env ops = some final ∧
      AddressWords width initial final := by
  refine ⟨finalState width initial, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [run, step, addressCalculation, Instruction.execute, Operand.read,
      Operand64.read, State.write64, finalState, hpc, hactive]
  · constructor <;> simp [finalState, State.write64, hpc]
